goal: Allow an organization owner or admin to invite a colleague by email so the colleague can join the organization, with the colleague joining only by an explicit action of their own.

authorship.reason: The product agent could not be dispatched: the orchestrator subagent type was unavailable in the session, so no agent could reach the specification stage. The eight product decisions recorded in task.yaml under product_decisions are the human's own answers; this file folds them into acceptance criteria, business rules and edge cases. No decision here was invented by the author.

actors.name: organization owner
actors.description: Full control of the organization, including billing

actors.name: organization member
actors.description: A regular member with no membership-management rights

actors.name: invited colleague
actors.description: The person named by an invitation. May already hold an account, or may not be registered yet.
permissions: accept the invitation addressed to their own email address

actors.name: unrelated signed-in user
actors.description: A signed-in user whose email address is not the invited address
permissions: may load an invitation link, but may not accept it

user_stories.story: As an organization owner or admin, I want to invite a colleague by email address, so that they can join the organization without me setting up their access manually.
As an invited colleague, I want to review an invitation and then accept it deliberately, so that I am not added to an organization without my knowledge.
As an organization owner, I want an invitation to stop working after a bounded period, so that an unused invitation does not remain a way in indefinitely.
As an organization admin, I want to be able to re-invite a colleague whose email went astray, so that I can recover without a dedicated resend feature.

acceptance_criteria.text: An organization owner or admin can send an invitation naming an email address, and the resulting invitation refers to that address and to the organization in whose context it was created.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Send an invitation as an owner and again as an admin; observe an invitation created that names the invited address and that organization.

acceptance_criteria.text: A regular member cannot invite a colleague and cannot cause a colleague to join the organization by attempting it.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Attempt to invite as a regular member and observe refusal, with no invitation created and no membership granted.

acceptance_criteria.text: The invited address receives an email containing a link that identifies the invitation and that does not itself grant membership.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Send an invitation; confirm exactly one message was delivered to the invited address, and that loading its link grants no membership.

acceptance_criteria.text: A colleague joins the organization only after an explicit accept action by a person whose email address is the invited address.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Load the invitation link without accepting and confirm no membership exists; then accept as the invited address and confirm a membership is created.

acceptance_criteria.text: A signed-in user whose email address differs from the invited address cannot accept the invitation and does not join the organization by attempting it.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: While signed in as a different address, attempt to accept an invitation and observe refusal with no membership created for either party.

acceptance_criteria.text: An invitation expires 7 days after it is created, and after expiry it cannot be accepted.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Create an invitation, advance time beyond 7 days, attempt to accept, and observe refusal with no membership created.

acceptance_criteria.text: A refusal to accept an invitation is indistinguishable across the states unknown, malformed, expired, and already accepted.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Compare the response and observable behaviour across the four states; they must not be distinguishable from one another.

acceptance_criteria.text: An invitation can be accepted at most once, including when acceptance is attempted twice at the same time.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Accept an invitation, then attempt again and observe refusal. Then create a fresh invitation and issue concurrent acceptances; observe exactly one success.

acceptance_criteria.text: The colleague joins as a regular member and receives no elevated permissions as a result of being invited.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Accept an invitation and confirm the resulting membership carries the regular member role and no administrative capability.

acceptance_criteria.text: Inviting an address that is already a member of the organization does not create a second membership.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Invite an existing member, accept, and confirm exactly one membership exists for that address and organization.

acceptance_criteria.text: When an invitation is already outstanding for the same organization and email address, sending a new invitation leaves exactly one outstanding invitation, and the earlier one can no longer be accepted.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Send two invitations for the same address and organization; confirm the earlier invitation is refused on acceptance and that only one invitation can be accepted successfully.

acceptance_criteria.text: An invitation is created for the organization identified in the request, and a caller who holds no owner or admin role in that organization cannot create one for it.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: As a user who is an admin of one organization and only a member of another, attempt to invite in each; observe success only where the caller holds owner or admin.

acceptance_criteria.text: A colleague who does not yet hold an account can be invited, and can complete joining, without an account existing when the invitation is created.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Invite an address with no account, then join from that address and confirm the membership is created.

acceptance_criteria.text: When an invitation cannot be delivered to the invited address, the colleague does not join and the invitation is not left apparently usable.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Cause delivery to fail and confirm no membership results and that the outstanding invitation cannot be accepted as though delivery had succeeded.

business_rules.rule: Only an owner or admin of an organization may create an invitation for that organization.
business_rules.rationale: A membership is a grant of access to organization data, so the power to create one must match the power to manage membership.

business_rules.rule: An invitation is valid for 7 days from its creation and cannot be accepted after that.
business_rules.rationale: Bounds how long a leaked invitation remains useful. 7 days is a chosen default, not a measured optimum.

business_rules.rule: An invitation is bound to the email address it names and is not transferable to any other address.
business_rules.rationale: Consent to join must come from the person who was invited.

business_rules.rule: Joining requires an explicit accept action by the invited person. Merely loading the invitation link never grants membership.
business_rules.rationale: Mail clients, link scanners and chat previews fetch links automatically. If loading accepted, the invitation would be consumed before the colleague ever saw it.

business_rules.rule: An invitation is single-use: accepting it consumes it, and concurrent acceptance attempts produce exactly one success.
At most one invitation may be outstanding for the same organization and email address. Creating a new one invalidates the outstanding one.
business_rules.rationale: Keeps acceptance unambiguous and bounds what a leaked invitation can do, while letting an admin recover from a lost email without a dedicated resend feature.

business_rules.rule: A colleague who is already a member of the organization cannot be added a second time by an invitation.
business_rules.rationale: Membership is a single relationship; a duplicate row would corrupt role resolution.

business_rules.rule: An invitation grants the regular member role and never an administrative role.
business_rules.rationale: Least privilege. An invitation that could grant admin would let a mistake or a malicious invite silently escalate access.

business_rules.rule: The invitation token is a credential and must not be stored in a form from which it can be recovered.
business_rules.rationale: A read of the persistence layer must not become a way to join an organization.

business_rules.rule: Refusals to accept an invitation do not reveal which refusal reason applies.
business_rules.rationale: Distinguishable refusals turn the accept path into an oracle for which invitations exist.

edge_cases.expected: refused; response and behaviour identical to the unknown-invitation case

edge_cases.case: an invitation is already outstanding for the same organization and address
edge_cases.expected: the earlier invitation can no longer be accepted; exactly one invitation is outstanding

edge_cases.case: the invited address is already a member of the organization
the same invitation is accepted twice at the same moment
edge_cases.expected: exactly one acceptance succeeds and exactly one membership results

edge_cases.case: a signed-in user whose address is not the invited address attempts to accept
edge_cases.expected: refused; the invitation remains acceptable by the invited address

edge_cases.case: a caller who holds no role in the target organization attempts to invite
edge_cases.expected: refused, with no invitation created for that organization

edge_cases.case: a caller who is an admin in organization A attempts to invite into organization B where they are only a member
edge_cases.expected: refused for B; success remains possible for A

edge_cases.case: the invitation token is unknown, malformed, empty, or of the wrong shape
edge_cases.expected: refused; indistinguishable from the expired case and never an error that discloses internal state

edge_cases.case: a mail client, link scanner or chat preview fetches the invitation link
edge_cases.expected: no membership is granted and the invitation remains acceptable afterwards

edge_cases.case: the invitation email cannot be delivered
edge_cases.expected: the colleague does not join, and no invitation is left that appears usable

edge_cases.case: the invited address is not yet a registered user
edge_cases.expected: the invitation is created and can be completed by that address

edge_cases.case: the email address is unusual but valid
edge_cases.expected: accepted, and matched consistently with the project's existing address handling so that duplicate and already-member checks agree with it

edge_cases.case: the organization named in the invitation request does not exist or the caller cannot see it
edge_cases.expected: refused; no invitation and no membership created

edge_cases.case: the invited address is empty or absent from the request

out_of_scope: creating, renaming, or deleting an organization
removing a member, or a member leaving an organization
changing a member's role after they have joined
inviting more than one colleague in a single action
a dedicated resend or cancel action (replacing an outstanding invitation covers the lost-email case)
seat limits, billing, or subscription checks on invitations
invitation analytics, audit history, or reporting
organization roles beyond owner, admin or member

assumptions.assumption: The project already has a working transactional email transport that the invitation can use.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: email delivery becomes a separate task, and AC-3 and AC-14 depend on it.

assumptions.assumption: An organization can already be identified and the caller's role in it can already be determined.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: AC-12 and BR-1 depend on an authorization mechanism that would have to be built first.

assumptions.assumption: A person with no account can be guided through account creation as part of joining.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: AC-13 cannot be satisfied and invitations could only be sent to existing users.

assumptions.assumption: Address matching for the duplicate and already-member checks uses the project's existing address handling, so a case variant of the same address is treated as the same address.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: AC-10 and AC-11 could be defeated by sending the same address with different capitalisation.
